title: Composite paper and paperboard, not surface-coated or impregnated

review.classification: A flat roll or sheet formed by adhesive bonding of flat paper/paperboard plies falls under the selected composite-paper scope where surface coating and impregnation are excluded. Cross-check HS 4807, the dimensions/form requirement and the actual surfaces. Wet-couched board, corrugated material, foil or plastic laminates and fabricated box/mount articles have different boundaries. The product name or use in conservation is insufficient on its own.
review.primary_evidence: The commercial ES flat multi-ply, starch-bonded family supports the narrow material identity. The original historical Strathmore photographic case separately observes dried single-ply rolls passing to a finishing site for bonding, staged storage/drying and cutting into sheets. A contemporary converter reports bonding rolls, including customer-provided materials. Do not equate a cross-facility transfer with a purchase or infer an adhesive formulation, contemporary utility rate or an uncoated specification for a particular lot.
review.measurement: Measure first accepted original flat-board net mass at stated moisture, excluding wrap. Opening finished stock, genuine returns or reinspection cannot add a second production acceptance. Dry solids and water need separate evidence for non-water volatile content. Incoming supplied adhesive includes its own water; only independently metered additional water counts as an additional input. Cutting fractions, external dust and accepted offcuts are distinct. Book original metered energy and verify the provider’s native delivery basis. Preserve packaging purchases, first nonpurchase receipts, true returns, outward movements and remaining burden vectors. A new purchase, a free first receipt and a return have distinct acquisition/burden histories.
review.readiness: Candidate methodology only; the exact board and process exchanges, site balances, conditions of the selected converter and applicable upstream providers are study-specific. A material-level association does not establish scientific approval or publication.
review.bilingual_and_projection: The aligned English and Chinese contain 19 atomic exchange cards each. The uniquely linked board_output is the one kilogram net reference. The precise product-flow UUID is documented as unresolved under the candidate methodology contract. The focused check covers 98 measurement items with none skipped. Amount-range warnings remain where independent quantitative bounds have yet to be established.
review.author_draft_integrity: All four final author blobs match the recorded independently checked repair draft byte for byte. The original local author commit is retained for traceability.

sources.first_title_line: Composite paper and paperboard, not surface-coated or impregnated

sources.role: CPC3 row 1276, classification metadata only. This subclass is defined through the following headings/subheadings of HS 2022: 4807.

JRC 2015, Pulp, Paper and Board BREF, §7.1.10 p. 670 (PDF p. 708) and §7.1.11.5 p. 677 (PDF p. 715). Original complete document SHA-256 bec1969fc48038bb4ad505cc2dabca577eeab178ff99efffdbbebf85ab83cbd0. Finishing supports qualitative cutting and wrapping; wet machine forming and recirculation are outside the dry-converter gate.

Producer sheet confirms identifiable multi-ply dyed-through starch-bonded material and neutral/synthetic sizing. Confirm actual outer surfaces and layer state. Sizing alone does not establish location, coating or lack of impregnation.
Same maker differentiates wet couching from adhesives and multiple possible surface grades.

Independent producer expressly describes an uncoated product and multilayer starch bonding above a specific grammage. Construction is in the paper machine. This is a real adjacent route, but cannot prove the selected converter used already dry purchased plies or duplicate that converter inventory.

HS 4807.00 identifies adhesive between flat layers and excludes coating and impregnation of the surface. Actual conversion/cut shape and rolls or sheets requirements apply; a finished storage box or actual artwork mount is a different item.

Henry Wilhelm and Carol Brower, The Permanence and Care of Color Photographs, chapter 13, printed pages 463–465, original 1988 photographic case. Earlier manufactured single-ply museum-board rolls are brought to a separate finishing site; starch adhesive, joining, drying, rewinding or cutting, and finished sheets are observed. Staged two-ply stock can be a four-ply input. This cross-facility case supports a physical conversion boundary but cannot establish an external purchase, present supplier, actual study grade, impacts or quantitative values.

Converter’s reel-to-sheet lamination and contract-laminating descriptions. A separate converter stocks finished reels and can also bond materials supplied by a customer. Physical receipt and ownership/payment can differ. Glue identity, actual faces and coating status of a particular grade need independent evidence.

ES-products description and product family. The producer identifies heat-treated-starch bonding of two or more flat plies; this supports the binder and product family. It cannot establish source-specific zero site emissions or exact conversion inputs.

Manufacturer original product listing confirms the natural-white multiple-ply flat-sheet variants and their unit of sale. Use documented supplied form, surfaces and treatment for actual applicability.
